also: because I want it that way

terms.gloss: because I feel like it; because I say so
evidence: Plaut. Bacch. 751: Quia mī ita lubet.
terms.comment: The curt answer of comedy when the speaker will give no reason: Simo, asked why, answers only quia libet. Plautus has the older spelling lubet.

terms.gloss: I said no; no means no
evidence: Plaut. Most. 1176: Nōlō ōrēs. — Quaesō hercle. — Nōlō, inquam, ōrēs.
terms.comment: Inquam repeats what has been said already, with weight: “I tell you”, “I said”.

phrases.latin: Obsecrō, quid istīs ad istunc ūsust cōnscrīptīs modum … ? — Quia mī ita lubet.
phrases.english: For heaven’s sake, what’s the use of writing it that way …? — Because that’s how I want it.

phrases.latin: Nōlō ōrēs. — Quaesō hercle. — Nōlō, inquam, ōrēs.
phrases.english: Don’t beg. — Please, for heaven’s sake! — I said, don’t beg.

phrases.latin: Nōn licet. Nōlō, inquam; nōlī amplius rogāre.
phrases.english: You may not. I said no; stop asking.

sources: Lewis & Short: libet · Lewis & Short: inquam
